## Client management
### Clients aren't able download content from CMG when branch cache is enabled
*Applies to: version 2403*
After Branch Cache is enabled on primary sites, clients are unable to download apps and packages from the cloud management gateway (CMG). They typically manage to download only 20-30% of the content before the process gets stuck. In some cases, after downloading certain blocks of packages from the CMG, clients look for Branch Cache to retrieve the remaining content. However, none of the clients are able to download the complete content from the CMG, which prevents others from using Branch Cache to access it. The **CTM.log** on the client includes entries similar to the following:
```log
(CTM.log - CTMJob({63B4C4CE-2DC4-4062-93C7-E5019B3B6CE1}): CCTMJob::Start - State=DownloadingContentFromPeers)
CTM.log _- CTMJob({D21758B0-D895-474E-9695-1023A25A1770}): CCTMJob::_PerformDownloadWithOutBranchCache - Download failure using branchcache, fallback to regular download
To work around this issue, disable branch cache.
> [!NOTE]
>
> Clients are able to download content from the on-premises distribution point when Branch Cache is enabled.

## Set up and upgrade
### ODBC driver version 18.7.1.1 can block site configuration before updating to 2609
*Applies to: upgrades to version 2609*
Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server version [18.7.1.1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/windows/release-notes-odbc-sql-server-windows#187) has a known issue with Configuration Manager version 2603 and earlier that can block site configuration.
To avoid this issue, don't install ODBC driver version 18.7.1.1 before updating Configuration Manager. Use ODBC driver version [18.6.2.1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/windows/release-notes-odbc-sql-server-windows#186), the validated version shipped with Configuration Manager 2609, for the update. Complete the Configuration Manager update to version 2609 before you install ODBC driver version 18.7.1.1.

For more information, see [ODBC driver for SQL Server](list-of-prerequisite-checks.md#odbc-driver-for-sql-server).

### Configuration Manager performance counters are missing on Windows Server 2025

*Applies to: primary site servers and management points running Windows Server 2025*

On Windows Server 2025, Configuration Manager performance counter registration can fail, leaving the counters unavailable in Performance Monitor. This issue can occur after a clean installation of Windows Server 2025 or an in-place upgrade from Windows Server 2022.

- **Unable to open the console because extension installation loops**
  In certain circumstances, you're unable to open the console due to an extension installation loop. This issue occurs when two or more versions of a single extension are marked as [required for installation](../../core/servers/manage/admin-console-extensions.md#require-installation-of-a-console-extension). This issue can occur for extensions imported through the wizard, from a PowerShell script, or through Community hub. To prevent the issue, use the **Make optional** setting before importing a new version of the extension.

  When this issue occurs, it initially appears as a normal console extension installation. After the extension finishes installing, you select **Close** to restart the Configuration Manager console. When the console restarts, you're prompted to install the console extension again. The extension installation continues to loop, and the Configuration Manager console doesn't fully open.

  To prevent and work around this issue in previous versions of Configuration Manager, run the following SQL script on your CAS database and all your primary site databases:

  ```sql
  ALTER VIEW vSMS_ConsoleExtensionMetadata
  AS
      WITH m AS(
         SELECT *,
             RN = ROW_NUMBER()OVER(PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Version DESC)
         FROM ConsoleExtensionMetadata
      )
      SELECT
          m.ID,
          m.Name,
          m.Description,
          m.Author,
          m.Version,
          m.IsEnabled,
          m.IsApproved,
          m.CreatedTime,
          m.CreatedBy,
          m.UpdateTime,
          m.IsTombstoned,
          m.IsRequired,
          m.IsSigned,
          m.IsUnsignedAllowed,

updates.title: Set up the Enrollment Status Page
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “ESP tracking”. Compare the added wording and its surrounding context below.
updates.after:
### PowerShell script execution during ESP

PowerShell scripts can run while the Enrollment Status Page (ESP) is displayed. However, ESP doesn't track PowerShell scripts as blocking workloads or wait for them to complete successfully. ESP can complete when its tracked applications and policies meet the configured ESP criteria, even if a PowerShell script is still running.

At startup, the Intune management extension processes PowerShell scripts first, then starts Win32 app processing in the same startup flow. This ordering doesn't guarantee that all PowerShell scripts finish before any Win32 app processing begins. Other device check-ins or notifications can independently trigger app processing while a script is still running.

Don't rely on ESP or the Intune management extension startup order to ensure that a PowerShell script completes before a Win32 app starts installing. If an app requires a script or another prerequisite to complete before installation, include that prerequisite as part of the Win32 app deployment.

# Become a Microsoft Intune Mobile Device Management Partner

The Third-Party Compliance MDM Partner Program is designed for mobile device management (MDM) solutions that determine and manage compliance for user-associated devices and use Microsoft Entra ID to communicate device compliance status to Microsoft services.

## Supported scenarios

To be eligible as an Intune compliance partner, your MDM solution must meet the following criteria:

- Manage devices using MDM protocols.
- Evaluate device compliance for user-based scenarios.
- Use Microsoft Entra ID for user identification.
- Support one or more of the following platforms: Android, iOS/iPadOS, and macOS.

## Apply to become an Intune compliance MDM partner

Partners interested in integrating with Microsoft should begin by creating a Microsoft Entra app for their MDM product. For instructions, see [Register a Microsoft Entra app and create a service principal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-create-service-principal-portal).

After you create a Microsoft Entra app and obtain a Microsoft Entra app ID, you can apply to become a partner through the [Intune Compliance MDM Partner Application](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/GKYuFnrSdv).

Microsoft uses the submitted information to validate that:

- The solution aligns with the intended Intune and Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access scenario.
- The proposed integration is appropriate for the Intune Device Compliance API.
- The partner is prepared to provide enterprise-grade support to customers after launch.

To protect your organization and customers, do not include detailed implementation information, source code, API payloads, security internals, proprietary design details, or other information not reasonably necessary for Microso

updates.after:
> Include the HTTP or HTTPS prefix in the proxy address. This requirement differs from previous versions of the connector.
   >
   > The proxy settings configured in the Certificate Connector wizard apply to the connector services. They don't configure the system-wide Windows HTTP Services (WinHTTP) proxy.
   >
   > If your environment also requires a WinHTTP proxy, configure it separately. Changing the system-wide WinHTTP proxy can affect other applications and services that use the default WinHTTP proxy configuration. Review any changes with your network administrator.

   If your environment requires a system-wide static WinHTTP proxy, use the following procedure:

   1. Open **Command Prompt as administrator**. Before making changes, display and record the existing configuration:

      ```cmd
      netsh winhttp show proxy
      ```
   2. Configure the proxy. The following example sets a static proxy and bypass list. Replace the server, port, and bypass entries with values approved for your environment:

      ```cmd
      netsh winhttp set proxy proxy-server="proxy.contoso.com:8080" bypass-list="<local>;*.contoso.com"
      ```

      The bypass list allows direct connections to short-name hosts and hosts matching `*.contoso.com`.
   3. Verify the resulting configuration:

      ```cmd
      netsh winhttp show proxy
      ```

   To remove the configured proxy and use direct connections, run the following command only if direct connectivity is intended:

   ```cmd
   netsh winhttp reset proxy
   ```

   Resetting the proxy doesn't restore a previous proxy configuration and can interrupt connectivity where a proxy is required.

updates.title: Automatic registration of existing devices
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Requirements; Windows Autopilot for existing devices”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
An existing device can automatically register if it's:
- Running a [supported version](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/release-information/) of Windows
For devices that meet these requirements, the MDM service can ask the device for the hardware hash. After it has that, it can automatically register the device with Windows Autopilot.
For more information on how to automatically register devices for Windows Autopilot with Microsoft Intune, see [Create a Windows Autopilot deployment profile](profiles.md#create-a-windows-autopilot-deployment-profile) and review the description of the **Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot** setting. See the following example:
> Using the setting **Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot** in the Windows Autopilot profile doesn't automatically convert existing hybrid Microsoft Entra device in the assigned groups into a Microsoft Entra device. The setting only registers the devices in the assigned groups for the Windows Autopilot service. For more information, see [Create a Windows Autopilot deployment profile](profiles.md#create-a-windows-autopilot-deployment-profile).
When the [Windows Autopilot for existing devices](existing-devices.md) scenario is used, devices don't need to be preregistered with Windows Autopilot. Instead, a configuration file (AutopilotConfigurationFile.json) containing all the Windows Autopilot profile settings is used. The device can then be registered with Windows Autopilot using the same **Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot** setting.
- [Registration overview](registration-overview.md).
updates.after:
An existing device can automatically register if it meets the following criteria:
- Runs a [supported version](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/release-information/) of Windows
For devices that meet these requirements, the MDM service can request the hardware hash from the device. After it has the hardware hash, it can automatically register the device with Windows Autopilot.
For more information about how to automatically register devices for Windows Autopilot with Microsoft Intune, see [Create a Windows Autopilot deployment profile](profiles.md#create-a-windows-autopilot-deployment-profile) and review the description of the **Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot** setting. See the following example:
> Using the **Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot** setting in the Windows Autopilot profile doesn't automatically convert existing hybrid Microsoft Entra devices in the assigned groups into Microsoft Entra devices. The setting only registers the devices in the assigned groups for the Windows Autopilot service. For more information, see [Create a Windows Autopilot deployment profile](profiles.md#create-a-windows-autopilot-deployment-profile).
When you use the [Windows Autopilot for existing devices](existing-devices.md) scenario, you don't need to preregister devices with Windows Autopilot. Instead, use a configuration file (AutopilotConfigurationFile.json) that contains the Windows Autopilot profile settings. You can then register the device with Windows Autopilot by using the **Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot** setting.
- [Registration overview](registration-overview.md)

updates.title: OEM registration
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Device registration process”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
When devices are purchased from an OEM, the OEM can automatically register the devices with the Windows Autopilot. For the list of OEMs that support registration, see the **Participant device manufacturers and resellers** section of the [Windows Autopilot page](https://aka.ms/windowsautopilot).
> While the hardware hashes, also known as hardware IDs, are generated as part of the OEM device manufacturing process, the hardware hashes aren't normally provided directly to customers or Cloud Solution Partners (CSPs). Instead, the OEM should register devices on the customer's behalf. In cases where CSPs register devices, OEMs might provide PKID information to those partners to support the device registration process.
OEMs must follow [device guidelines](autopilot-device-guidelines.md) for Windows Autopilot devices.
Microsoft manages and maintains Windows Autopilot. This service provides the backend database that associates hardware hashes with customer tenants. When an OEM registers devices for a customer, they're writing that data to this database and not directly to the customer's tenant. No permissions to the customer's tenant are granted or required for OEMs to register devices on the customer's behalf.
Before an OEM can register devices for an organization, the organization's Microsoft Entra Global Administrator must approve the OEM. For more information, see [OEM authorization](registration-auth.md#oem-authorization).
updates.after:

updates.title: Reseller, distributor, or partner registration
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Related content”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
Customers can purchase devices from resellers, distributors, or other partners. As long as these resellers, distributors, and partners are part of the [Cloud Solution Partners (CSP) program](https://partner.microsoft.com/cloud-solution-provider), they too can register devices for the customer.
As with OEMs, CSP partners must be granted permission to register devices for an organization. This process is described in the [CSP authorization](registration-auth.md#csp-authorization) section of the Windows Autopilot customer consent article. In summary:

- How you sign in, using workplace credentials

updates.before:
When you enroll your device for work or school use, you might need to adjust the lock screen and startup settings you use to unlock your device so that they align with your organization's password and biometric requirements. Password and biometric requirements are put in place to prevent unauthorized individuals from gaining access to the work or school data on your device. Until you choose a more secure authentication method for your device's lock screen, you might be blocked from accessing your organization's network.
For a list of all passcode-related messages in Company Portal, see [Device password messages in Company Portal](ref-password-messages.md). Company Portal sends you one message per password requirement. For example, if your passcode is too short and too simple, you receive one message about the length and one message about the complexity. Your workplace chooses the password and biometric requirements for your device. If the Company Portal messages appear too vague, contact your IT support person directly for the exact password and biometric requirements for your device.
- If you still receive password and authentication-related messages after updating your settings, try restarting your device.

This document offers guidance for Windows Autopilot device repair scenarios that Microsoft partners can use in motherboard replacement situations, and other servicing scenarios.
Repairing Windows Autopilot enrolled devices is complex, as it tries to balance OEM requirements with Windows Autopilot requirements. Specifically, OEM requirements include strict uniqueness across motherboards, MAC addresses, etc. Windows Autopilot requires strict uniqueness at the hardware hash level for each device to enable successful registration. The hardware hash doesn't always accommodate all the OEM hardware component requirements. These requirements are sometimes at odds, which can cause issues with some repair scenarios. The hardware hash is also known as the hardware ID.

- If the **IT Admin** registered the device, they likely did so via Intune, [Microsoft 365 admin center](https://admin.microsoft.com/), or a legacy portal such as Microsoft Store for Business (MSfB). updates.title: Overview of Windows Autopilot device preparation
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Windows Autopilot device preparation improvements; Improved experiences”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
- **Support for Government Community Cloud High (GCCH) and Department of Defense (DoD) environments**. Windows Autopilot device preparation supports [GCCH and DoD](../../intune/fundamentals/government-service.md) environments.
Windows Autopilot device preparation supports device association, which binds a physical Windows 11 device to your tenant before enrollment. Associated devices are automatically marked as corporate-owned and can receive device-targeted policy assignments and additional OOBE customizations. For more information, see [Overview of Windows Autopilot device association](device-association/overview.md).
updates.after:
### Cloud environments

Windows Autopilot device preparation supports [Government Community Cloud High (GCCH) and Department of Defense (DoD)](../../intune/fundamentals/government-service.md) environments.

The device association capability isn't yet available in sovereign cloud environments.
Device association uses a device's Trusted Platform Module (TPM)-backed identity to establish a trusted relationship with your tenant before enrollment. The association is stored in the device's Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) firmware and verified during onboarding.

Use device association to:

- Assign a device preparation policy directly to a device, regardless of which user signs in. A device-based policy assignment takes precedence over a user-based assignment.
- Automatically mark the device as corporate-owned.
- Apply a device name template during enrollment.
- Customize OOBE settings, such as language and keyboard configuration, and hide selected setup pages.

Device association is optional. For the full capabilities and lifecycle, see [Overview of Windows Autopilot device association](device-association/overview.md).

updates.before: - Installing apps up to the number of licenses you own.
updates.after:
- Installing apps up to the number of licenses you own, or without a fixed license quantity for apps with unlimited licenses.

### Unlimited assets

Intune supports assigning VPP apps with unlimited licenses from Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager on iOS/iPadOS and macOS devices. For these apps, you don't need to acquire additional license quantities as your deployment grows.

Apple refers to apps and books that an organization owns as *assets*. Free apps and books support unlimited assignment by default. However, organizations can choose to retain their existing fixed inventory for an organizational unit. Don't assume that every free app has unlimited licenses for every location. Paid apps still require sufficient purchased licenses for your assignments.

To deploy an app with unlimited licenses:

1. In Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager, acquire the free app for the location associated with your Intune location token.
2. In the Intune admin center, select **Tenant administration** > **Connectors and tokens** > **Apple VPP tokens**, select the token, and choose **Sync**. For more information, see [Synchronize a VPP token](#synchronize-a-vpp-token).
3. Assign the synchronized app to your groups as described in [Assign a volume-purchased app](#assign-a-volume-purchased-app).

Unlimited licenses remove the need to manage a fixed license quantity. They don't change the device and user licensing requirements or assignment restrictions described in this article.

updates.title: What is co-management?
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Benefits; Prerequisites”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
Co-management is one of the primary ways to attach your existing Configuration Manager deployment to the Microsoft 365 cloud. It helps you unlock more cloud-powered capabilities like Conditional Access.
You're also able to pilot a workload with a separate collection of devices. Piloting allows you to test the Intune functionality with a subset of devices before switching a larger group.
[![Overview diagram of co-management.](media/co-management-overview.svg)](media/co-management-overview.svg#lightbox)
> When you concurrently manage devices with both Configuration Manager and Microsoft Intune, this configuration is called *co-management*. When you manage devices with Configuration Manager and enroll to a third-party MDM service, this configuration is called *coexistence*. Having two management authorities for a single device can be challenging if not properly orchestrated between the two. With co-management, Configuration Manager and Intune balance the [workloads](#workloads) to make sure there are no conflicts. This interaction doesn't exist with third-party services, so there are limitations with the management capabilities of coexistence. For more information, see [Third-party MDM coexistence with Configuration Manager](coexistence.md).
When you enroll existing Configuration Manager clients in co-management, you gain the following immediate value:
- Intune-based remote actions, for example: restart, remote control, or factory reset
For more information on this immediate value from co-management, see the quickstarts series to [Cloud connect with co-management](quickstarts.md).

## Configure Azure RBAC permissions for the server app

The CMG uses the **server/web application's service principal** to deploy and manage its Azure resources. These Azure role-based access control (RBAC) permissions are separate from the Microsoft Entra directory roles used to create app registrations. Assign permissions to the server application's service principal, not the native/client application or the user who runs the console.

Starting in version 2609, shared-key access is automatically disabled for CMG storage. Existing CMGs that previously used shared-key access also need the permissions for Microsoft Entra-authenticated storage and storage role assignments. A successful deployment or update on an earlier version doesn't confirm that these permissions are present.

Verify the following effective permissions at each CMG resource group:

- **Resource management:** Retain the **Contributor** role or equivalent approved permissions that allow the server application to manage the CMG resources.
- **Storage role assignments:** Allow the server application to manage assignments of the **Storage Blob Data Contributor** and **Storage Table Data Contributor** roles. Contributor alone doesn't grant `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write`.

To provide the storage role-assignment permissions with limited delegation:

1. In the Azure portal, open the CMG's resource group and select **Access control (IAM)**.
2. Identify the service principal for the CMG server application. Verify its application (client) ID and service-principal object ID against the application used by Configuration Manager.
3. Review its existing role assignments, including inherited assignments and their conditions. If equivalent effective permissions already exist, don't add a duplicate grant.

articles.title: About discovery methods for Configuration Manager

before.text: - To discover a computer resource by using Active Directory system discovery, the discovery agent must be able to resolve the FQDN of the resource. If it can't resolve the FQDN, it then tries to resolve the resource by its NetBIOS name.

- To discover a user or group resource by using Active Directory user discovery or Active Directory group discovery, the discovery agent must be able to resolve the FQDN of the domain controller name that you specify for the Active Directory location.

For each location that you specify, you can configure individual search options, like enabling a recursive search of the location's Active Directory child containers. You can also configure a unique account to use when it searches that location. This account provides flexibility in configuring a discovery method at one site to search multiple Active Directory locations across multiple forests. You don't have to configure a single account that has permissions to all locations.

When each of these three discovery methods runs at a specific site, the Configuration Manager site server at that site contacts the nearest domain controller in the specified Active Directory forest to locate Active Directory resources. The domain and forest can be in any supported Active Directory mode. The account that you assign to each location instance must have **Read** access permission to the specified Active Directory locations.

# Bulk registration token verification fails after installing Configuration Manager 2603 update rollup

*Applies to: Configuration Manager (current branch, version 2603 with update rollup KB39169655 installed)*

## Summary of KB40345593

This update resolves a token verification issue that occurs after you install the [update rollup for Microsoft Configuration Manager version 2603 (KB39169655)](39169655.md).

After you install the update rollup, bulk registration token verification fails on the management point for devices that aren't Microsoft Entra joined and connect through a cloud management gateway (CMG) to obtain a Configuration Manager-issued client authentication token.

This issue affects the [bulk registration token](../../core/clients/deploy/deploy-clients-cmg-token.md#bulk-registration-token) scenario and may also affect other scenarios in which devices that aren't Microsoft Entra joined communicate through the CMG. It doesn't affect devices that use Microsoft Entra authentication.

On the management point, errors similar to the following are recorded in `<MP_InstallDir>\Logs\CCM_STS.log`:

```text
ProcessRequest - Start
Incoming request URL: https://<management-point>/CCM_STS
Validated PreAuth SelfProve token. UniqueId: <client-id>. ClientKey: <public-key>
ProcessRequest - Exception: System.IO.FileLoadException:
Could not load file or assembly
'mpisapiclr, Version=5.0.9146.1045, Culture=neutral,
PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35' or one of its dependencies.
The located assembly's manifest definition does not match the assembly reference.
(Exception from HRESULT: 0x80131040)
```

As a result, affected devices can't complete bulk registration through the CMG to obtain their individual client authentication tokens.

  - Critical update
  - Firmware update
  - Configuration file update
  - All other updates (OS, built-in apps)
- Create a schedule that determines when the update installs. Schedules can be simple, like installing updates the next time that the device checks in. Or, you can create day-time ranges when updates can install or when they're blocked from installing.

By default, devices check in with [Intune about every 8 hours](../../device-configuration/troubleshoot-device-profiles.md#policy-refresh-intervals). If an update is available through an update policy, the device downloads the update. The device then installs the update upon next check-in within your schedule configuration.

On Android Enterprise devices, you can use the **General > Block location** in the [settings catalog](../device-configuration/settings-catalog/ref-android-settings.md) to disable the location services on the device and prevent users from turning it on.
This setting is now called **Location** and has three options you can configure:
- Device default - Intune doesn't change or update this setting. By default, the OS allows end users to turn location services on or off.
- Location enabled - Requires location services to be on and prevents end users from turning them off.
- Location disabled - Requires location services to be off and prevents end users from turning them on.
For a list of all the settings you can configure, see [Android Intune settings catalog settings list](../device-configuration/settings-catalog/ref-android-settings.md).

Previously, file elevation requests that require support approval were supported from only a device's primary user or the user who enrolled the device.

## Week of October 26, 2026 (Service release 2610)

### App management

#### Manage referenced apps on AOSP devices

Microsoft Intune now supports AOSP referenced app type that lets you identify an app by package name instead of uploading an APK on AOSP devices. You can assign Required or Uninstall intent to OEM, preloaded, or externally deployed apps that already exist on supported AOSP devices. Required makes an existing app unhidden, while Uninstall hides it. You'll also be able to target referenced apps with JSON-based app configuration policies; Configuration designer and Connected Apps won't be supported. This capability will help organizations manage device-resident apps without adding a new app distribution path.

Applies to:

- Android

### Device configuration

#### Enforce Routes capability in Apple VPN profiles

Microsoft Intune now supports Apple's Enforce Routes capability in iOS/iPadOS and macOS VPN profiles. Admins define routing behavior with **Include all networks** and **Exclude local networks**, and Intune automatically derives the appropriate Enforce Routes configuration. This helps reduce VPN traffic bypass and de-cloaking risks while keeping routing behavior consistent with Apple's platform semantics.

For more information, see [Add VPN settings to Apple devices in Microsoft Intune](../device-configuration/templates/ref-vpn-settings-apple.md).

Applies to:

- iOS/iPadOS
- macOS

#### Legacy Apple MDM software update workloads removed from Intune

Microsoft Intune is removing legacy Apple MDM software update workloads after Apple retired the underlying commands and payloads in OS 27. updates.before:
Your organization's IT admin uses Software Center to install applications, software updates, and upgrade Windows. This user guide explains the functionality of Software Center for users of the computer.
- Your IT admin may disable some aspects of Software Center. Your specific experience may vary.
- If multiple users are using a device at the same time, the user with the lowest session ID will be the only one to see all available deployments in Software Center. For example, multiple users on a remote desktop environment. Users with higher session IDs may not see some of the deployments in Software Center. For example, the users with higher session IDs may see deployed Applications, but not deployed Packages or Task Sequences. Meanwhile the user with the lowest session ID will see all deployed Applications, Packages, and Task Sequences. The **Users** tab of Windows Task Manager shows all users and their session IDs.

updates.before:
The **Pre-provision BitLocker** task sequence step in Configuration Manager allows you to enable BitLocker from the Windows Preinstallation Environment (Windows PE) prior to operating system deployment. Only the used drive space is encrypted, and therefore, encryption times are much faster. This is done with a randomly generated clear protector applied to the formatted volume and encrypting the volume prior to running the Windows setup process. The ability to pre-provision BitLocker was introduced with Windows 8 and Windows Server 2012. However, you can pre-provision BitLocker on a hard drive and install Windows 7 as long as you follow specific steps. After Windows 7 Setup completes, you must set a BitLocker key protector because the Windows 7 BitLocker control panel does not support BitLocker with a clear protector. You must add a key protector by using the **Enable BitLocker** step or by using the manage-bde.exe command-line tool.
Generally, you must do the following to successfully pre-provision BitLocker on a computer that will install Windows 7:
- Restart the computer in Windows PE
  > You must use a boot image with Windows PE 4 or later to pre-provision BitLocker. For more information about supported Windows PE versions in Configuration Manager, see [Dependencies External to Configuration Manager](../plan-design/infrastructure-requirements-for-operating-system-deployment.md#dependencies-external-to-configuration-manager).
- Install Windows 7 with specific operating system and network settings
- Add a key protector to BitLocker

updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Week of October 26, 2026”. Compare the added wording and its surrounding context below.
updates.after:
## Week of October 26, 2026

### Device management

#### Bulk manage eSIMs on corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices

Microsoft Intune now supports bulk eSIM actions for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices. From **Devices** > **All devices** > **Bulk device actions**, you can activate eSIMs on up to 100 selected devices running Android 15 or later by using a carrier activation server URL. Bulk eSIM activation is available only in the updated bulk device actions experience.

When you bulk wipe supported devices, Intune preserves eSIM data plans by default. You can select the option to remove eSIMs when the wipe should also remove the data plans. Personally owned Android Enterprise work profile devices aren't supported.

For more information, see [Activate eSIMs on multiple Android Enterprise devices](../device-management/actions/update-cellular-data-plan.md#activate-esims-on-multiple-android-enterprise-devices) and [Wipe multiple Android Enterprise devices](../device-management/actions/wipe.md#wipe-multiple-android-enterprise-devices).

Applies to:

- Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed devices (COBO)
- Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated devices (COSU)
- Android Enterprise corporate-owned devices with a work profile (COPE)

updates.title: Manage AOSP referenced apps in Microsoft Intune
updates.summary: This article was newly captured in the tracker. This does not establish when Microsoft first published it or released a feature.
updates.after:
# Manage AOSP referenced apps in Microsoft Intune

AOSP referenced apps identify apps by package name instead of an uploaded APK. You can use Microsoft Intune to manage OEM, preloaded, or externally deployed apps on Android Open Source Project (AOSP) devices. The app must already be on the device or be deployed outside Intune.

To unhide an existing app on the device, assign the referenced app as **Required**. To hide the app without deleting it, assign it as **Uninstall**. The **Available** assignment type isn't supported for referenced apps.

AOSP referenced apps support user-associated and userless AOSP devices.

## Before you start

- Make sure the devices are enrolled in Intune with AOSP user-associated or AOSP userless enrollment.
- Make sure the app is already on the devices, or arrange to deploy it outside Intune.
- Get the app's package name. If you don't know the package name, contact the device manufacturer or app vendor.
- Make sure you have permissions to create and assign apps in the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431). For permission guidance, see [Role-based access control](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/overview.md).

## Select the app type

Select the AOSP referenced app type to open the app creation steps. You don't need to upload an APK or select an app from Google Play.

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
2. Select **Apps** > **All apps** > **Create**.
3. For **Platform**, select **Android**.
4. For **Category**, select **Referenced apps**.
5. Select **AOSP referenced app**, and then select **Create**.

## Set app information

Enter the app details and the package name that Intune uses to identify the app on the device.

## VPN tunnel routing

Microsoft Intune supports Apple’s **Enforce Routes** capability in iOS/iPadOS and macOS VPN profiles. This enhancement helps administrators mitigate traffic bypass scenarios (such as de-cloaking risks) by ensuring VPN routing behavior aligns with Apple’s platform semantics.

This feature introduces a simplified configuration experience in the Intune admin center, where routing behavior is defined using **Include all networks** and **Exclude local networks** settings. Intune automatically derives the appropriate **Enforce Routes** configuration based on these selections to ensure consistent and predictable device behavior.

With this update:

- Intune supports Apple’s `enforceRoutes` capability for iOS/iPadOS and macOS VPN configurations.
- Routing behavior is explicitly modeled using:

  - **Include all networks**
  - **Exclude local networks**
- Intune automatically derives the correct `enforceRoutes` value based on the selected combination—removing the need for manual configuration.

This feature helps ensure that VPN routing behavior:

- Prevents unintended traffic leakage outside the VPN tunnel
- Aligns with Apple’s NetworkExtension routing model
- Provides consistent enforcement of routing policies across devices

In particular, enabling enforcement when required ensures that traffic does not bypass VPN routing due to local route precedence, which can otherwise lead to exposure of sensitive traffic.

**How routing behavior works**

Apple’s VPN model defines routing behavior using a combination of:

- Full tunnel behavior (**Include all networks**)
- Local network exceptions (**Exclude local networks**)
- Route precedence enforcement (**Enforce Routes**)

Intune simplifies this model by automatically deriving `enforceRoutes` when needed.

## VPN tunnel routing

Microsoft Intune supports Apple’s **Enforce Routes** capability in iOS/iPadOS and macOS VPN profiles. This enhancement helps administrators mitigate traffic bypass scenarios (such as de-cloaking risks) by ensuring VPN routing behavior aligns with Apple’s platform semantics.

This feature introduces a simplified configuration experience in the Intune admin center, where routing behavior is defined using **Include all networks** and **Exclude local networks** settings. Intune automatically derives the appropriate **Enforce Routes** configuration based on these selections to ensure consistent and predictable device behavior.
With this update:
- Intune supports Apple’s `enforceRoutes` capability for iOS/iPadOS and macOS VPN configurations.
- Routing behavior is explicitly modeled using:
- **Include all networks**
- **Exclude local networks**
- Intune automatically derives the correct `enforceRoutes` value based on the selected combination—removing the need for manual configuration.
This feature helps ensure that VPN routing behavior:
- Prevents unintended traffic leakage outside the VPN tunnel
- Aligns with Apple’s NetworkExtension routing model
- Provides consistent enforcement of routing policies across devices
In particular, enabling enforcement when required ensures that traffic does not bypass VPN routing due to local route precedence, which can otherwise lead to exposure of sensitive traffic.
**How routing behavior works**
Apple’s VPN model defines routing behavior using a combination of:
- Full tunnel behavior (**Include all networks**)
- Local network exceptions (**Exclude local networks**)
- Route precedence enforcement (**Enforce Routes**)
Intune simplifies this model by automatically deriving `enforceRoutes` when needed.
**Configuration and behavior**
| Include all networks | Exclude local networks | Enforce routes (derived) | Resulting device behavior |
| Off | Off | Off | Standard VPN routing based on configured routes |
| On | Off | Ignored | Most device traffic is routed through the VPN tunnel |
| On | On | Ignored | Most traffic is routed through the VPN, except local network traffic (for example, AirDrop, printers) |
| Off | On | On (auto-derived) | VPN routing is enforced, and local network traffic is excluded from the tunnel |
**Key behavior notes**
- When **Include all networks** is enabled, iOS routes most traffic through the VPN tunnel. In this scenario, Apple ignores the `enforceRoutes` setting.
- When **Exclude local networks** is enabled without **Include all networks**, Intune automatically enables **Enforce Routes** to ensure local network exclusions take effect.
- **Enforce Routes is only applied when required** and isn’t exposed as a standalone setting in the admin experience.
- These settings apply only to **device-wide VPN (tunnel routing)** configurations and aren’t applicable to **per-app VPN**.

- Using **split tunneling** together with **VPN tunnel routing** settings is not recommended. When **split tunneling** is enabled, it forces all traffic through the VPN at the system level and may override your configured routes.
**Security considerations**
By enforcing routing precedence when required:
- VPN traffic adheres to the configured routing policy
- Local device routes can’t override VPN-defined routing unexpectedly
Additional lines omitted.
::: zone pivot="ios-ipados"

updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Connector status”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, you can select a certificate connector to view information about its status:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431)
3. Select a connector to view its status.
   When viewing the connector status:
   - Deprecated connectors show a **Warning**. After the six-month grace period, the warning changes to an Error.
   - Connectors that are beyond the grace period show an Error. These connectors are no longer supported and can stop working at any time.
updates.after:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, the **Status** column displays the health of each certificate connector. To view the status and health messages for a connector:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
3. Select a connector to open its details pane.
The connector details pane displays the connector health status and any health messages that require your attention. Connector health status is based on recent certificate-processing activity. The most recently evaluated status is displayed for up to 15 minutes. If multiple issues are detected, the pane groups the messages by severity and provides guidance for each issue. A connector can display both **Action required** and **Warning** messages.
The following statuses are available:

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |

# Integrate an MDM provider with Windows Autopilot device association

Windows Autopilot device association can support integration with a mobile device management (MDM) provider other than Microsoft Intune. Provider integration is available through a limited-access onboarding process. Microsoft must authorize the Microsoft Entra application that the provider uses before the application can access the device association service.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> This process is for MDM providers that are building device association into their service. It doesn't provide an individual customer or administrator with direct access to the device association service.

## Prerequisites

Before requesting access, the MDM provider should:

- Support Windows device enrollment and management by using the Windows MDM protocols. For more information, see [Mobile Device Management overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm-overview).
- Integrate its MDM service with Microsoft Entra ID. For more information, see [Microsoft Entra integration with MDM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/azure-active-directory-integration-with-mdm).
- Register the Microsoft Entra application that the service uses to call device association APIs.
- Define how customers authorize the provider to perform device association operations for their tenant.

## Request access

Contact your Microsoft representative to request onboarding for Windows Autopilot device association. Include the following information:

- The provider's legal company name and MDM product name.
- Primary business and technical contacts.
- The Microsoft Entra tenant ID for the provider.
- The application (client) ID for each Microsoft Entra application and environment that requires access.
- A des

updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Prerequisites”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before: - CMPivot and the [Microsoft Edge](../../../apps/deploy-use/deploy-edge.md) installer are currently signed with the **Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2011** certificate. If you set PowerShell execution policy to **AllSigned**, then you need to make sure that devices trust this signing certificate. You can export the certificate from a computer where you've installed the Configuration Manager console. View the certificate on `"C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Endpoint Manager\AdminConsole\bin\CMPivot.exe"`, and then export the code signing certificate from the certification path. Then import it to the *machine*'s **Trusted Publishers** store on managed devices. You can use the process in the following blog, but make sure to export the *code signing certificate* from the certification path: [Adding a Certificate to Trusted Publishers using Intune](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/intune-customer-success/adding-a-certificate-to-trusted-publishers-using-intune/ba-p/1974488).
updates.after:
- CMPivot is currently signed with the **Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2011** certificate. If you set the PowerShell execution policy to **AllSigned**, devices must trust the certificate used to sign the CMPivot PowerShell script.

  - In [the update rollup for Configuration Manager version 2603](../../../hotfix/2603/39169655.md) or Configuration Manager version 2609 and later, the Configuration Manager client automatically adds the certificate to the *machine*'s **Trusted Publishers** store before the client runs the script. No manual action is required for CMPivot.
  - For earlier Configuration Manager versions, export the certificate from a computer where the Configuration Manager console is installed. View the certificate on `<AdminConsoleInstallDir>\bin\CMPivot.exe`, where `<AdminConsoleInstallDir>` is the Configuration Manager console installation folder. Export the code signing certificate from the certification path, and then import it to the *machine*'s **Trusted Publishers** store on managed devices. For an example, see [Adding a Certificate to Trusted Publishers using Intune](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/intune-customer-success/adding-a-certificate-to-trusted-publishers-using-intune/ba-p/1974488). Make sure to export the *code signing certificate* from the certification path.

updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Policy scope and user assignments; Create a Windows elevation settings policy”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
To configure Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) on devices, deploy *Windows elevation settings policy* to users or devices:
5. For **Assignments**, select the groups that receive the policy. For more information on assigning profiles, see [Assign user and device profiles](../device-configuration/assign-device-profile.md). Select **Next**.
updates.after:
To configure Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) on devices, deploy *Windows elevation settings policy* to groups that contain users or devices:

## Policy scope and user assignments

The *Windows elevation settings policy* configures the EPM client's settings. These client settings, including the default elevation response, are device-scoped and apply to all users on the device.

You can assign a *Windows elevation settings policy* to groups that contain users or devices. Assigning the policy to a group that contains users doesn't change the scope of its settings or create a separate default elevation response for each user. Once applied, the device-scoped configuration remains effective until another configuration is applied. Signing in as a different user doesn't, by itself, replace that configuration.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> Don't assign different *Windows elevation settings policies* to groups that contain users to switch the device's default elevation response between users. Instead, configure a consistent device-wide default and use elevation rules assigned to groups that contain users to define how specific applications can be elevated by those users. For more information, see [Deploying elevation rules](create-elevation-rules.md#deploying-rules-created-with-endpoint-privilege-management).
5. For **Assignments**, select the groups that receive the policy. For more information on assigning profiles, see [Assign user and device profiles](../device-configuration/assign-device-profile.md). Assigning this policy to a group that contains users doesn't make its settings user-scoped; see [Policy scope and user assignments](#policy-scope-and-user-assignments). Select **Next**.

#### Remote Help support for GCCH environments

Remote Help is now available in US Government Community Cloud High (GCCH) environments. This expansion extends the same secure, cloud-based remote assistance capabilities currently available in GCC to GCCH tenants.

IT support staff can establish Remote Help sessions with users on enrolled devices to provide real-time troubleshooting. Remote Help uses role-based access controls through Intune, and both helpers and sharers must sign in with their organization's Microsoft Entra ID accounts. DoD environments aren't supported.

For more information, see [Planning for Remote Help](../remote-help/plan.md).

Applies to:

- Android
- macOS
- Windows

### Apple OS 27 DDM status data in device inventory

Microsoft Intune will add Apple OS 27 declarative device management (DDM) status data to device inventory. You'll be able to review system health information for supported hardware components, content cache details, and MDM state such as enrollment type, awaiting configuration, Return to Service, Shared iPad, and Lockdown Mode. Reported values will depend on the device's supported operating system, hardware, enrollment type, and available DDM capabilities.

Intune will add support for the MEFERI OEMConfig app (`com.meferi.oemconfig`) for Android Enterprise devices. Once onboarded, admins will be able to use Intune's OEMConfig workflow to deploy and manage the device settings that MEFERI exposes through its OEM-provided schema. This update will expand the catalog of supported OEMConfig apps and reduce the need for custom management workarounds when organizations use MEFERI hardware. Admins will continue using the same OEMConfig pattern in Intune by adding the app from Managed Google Play, assigning it to devices, and creating OEMConfig profiles against the supported bundle.

updates.title: Set up automated device enrollment for iOS/iPadOS
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Create an Apple enrollment policy”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
13. If you select a token for **Install Company Portal with VPP**, you can lock the device in Single App Mode (specifically, the Company Portal app) right after the Setup Assistant completes. Select **Yes** for **Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication** to set this option. To use the device, the user must first authenticate by signing in to the Company Portal.

    > [!NOTE]
    >
    > Multifactor authentication isn't supported on a single device locked in Single App Mode. This limitation exists because the device can't switch to a different app to complete the second factor of authentication. If you want multifactor authentication on a Single App Mode device, the second factor must be on a different device.

    This feature is supported only for iOS/iPadOS 11.3.1 and later.

    ![Screenshot that shows the Run Company Portal in Single App Mode option.](media/setup-automated-ios/single-app-mode.png)
updates.after:
13. The **Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication** option is no longer supported and will soon be removed. This option must be set to **No**.

    > [!NOTE]
    >
    > The **Sync with computers** setting was deprecated by Apple in iOS 13 and is not included in enrollment policies.

updates.title: What's new in Microsoft Intune
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Week of September 28, 2026 (Service release 2609)”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
#### Bulk manage eSIMs on corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices

Microsoft Intune now supports bulk eSIM actions for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices. From **Devices** > **All devices** > **Bulk device actions**, you can activate eSIMs on up to 100 selected devices running Android 15 or later by using a carrier activation server URL.

When you bulk wipe supported devices, Intune preserves eSIM data plans by default. You can select the option to remove eSIMs when the wipe should also remove the data plans. Personally owned Android Enterprise work profile devices aren't supported.

Applies to:

- Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed devices (COBO)
- Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated devices (COSU)
- Android Enterprise corporate-owned devices with a work profile (COPE)
